review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

13:1.sourceText: Τρίτον τοῦτο ἔρχομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς· ἐπὶ στόματος δύο μαρτύρων καὶ τριῶν σταθήσεται πᾶν ῥῆμα.
13:1.targetText: This is the third time I am coming to you. “Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.”

groups.note: στόματος ("mouth") is rendered the testimony.
καί ("and") is rendered or.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek has none.

13:2.sourceText: προείρηκα καὶ προλέγω, ὡς παρὼν τὸ δεύτερον καὶ ἀπὼν νῦν, τοῖς προημαρτηκόσιν καὶ τοῖς λοιποῖς πᾶσιν, ὅτι ἐὰν ἔλθω εἰς τὸ πάλιν οὐ φείσομαι,
13:2.targetText: I already warned you the second time I was with you. So now in my absence I warn those who sinned earlier and everyone else: If I return, I will not spare anyone,

groups.note: The participle παρών ("being present") is rendered was with you.
καί ("and") is rendered So.
The participle ἀπών ("being absent") is rendered in my absence.
ἔλθω εἰς τὸ πάλιν ("I come again") is rendered I return.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB puts the two verbs in separate sentences and does not render this καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB introduces the warning with a colon instead of ὅτι ("that").

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object; the Greek verb has none.
A participle has no person; English supplies I.
English supplies with whom; the Greek has only παρών ("being present").
A participle has no person; English supplies my.
English supplies the object; the Greek verb has none.

13:3.sourceText: ἐπεὶ δοκιμὴν ζητεῖτε τοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ λαλοῦντος Χριστοῦ, ὃς εἰς ὑμᾶς οὐκ ἀσθενεῖ ἀλλὰ δυνατεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν.
13:3.targetText: since you are demanding proof that Christ is speaking through me. He is not weak in dealing with you, but is powerful among you.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the clause with that; the Greek has a genitive participle phrase.

13:4.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ ἐσταυρώθη ἐξ ἀσθενείας, ἀλλὰ ζῇ ἐκ δυνάμεως Θεοῦ. καὶ γὰρ ἡμεῖς ἀσθενοῦμεν ἐν αὐτῷ, ἀλλὰ ζήσομεν σὺν αὐτῷ ἐκ δυνάμεως Θεοῦ εἰς ὑμᾶς.
13:4.targetText: For He was indeed crucified in weakness, yet He lives by God’s power. And though we are weak in Him, yet by God’s power we will live with Him to serve you.

groups.note: ἐξ ("out of") is rendered in.
καὶ γάρ ("for indeed") is rendered And.
εἰς ὑμᾶς ("toward you") is rendered to serve you.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds though to pair with yet; the Greek has no concessive word.
English supplies the verb serve; the Greek has only εἰς ὑμᾶς ("toward you").

13:5.sourceText: Ἑαυτοὺς πειράζετε εἰ ἐστὲ ἐν τῇ πίστει, ἑαυτοὺς δοκιμάζετε· ἢ οὐκ ἐπιγινώσκετε ἑαυτοὺς ὅτι Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν; εἰ μήτι ἀδόκιμοί ἐστε.
13:5.targetText: Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith; test yourselves. Can’t you see for yourselves that Jesus Christ is in you—unless you actually fail the test?

groups.note: The actual Greek negation and plural recognition verb jointly form the English contracted negative question Cant you see. Its contraction cannot be assigned to overlapping artificial word pieces; the full negative predicate remains together.
The Greek reflexive direct object of recognize is recast as English for yourselves; the same actual reflexive participants remain linked with the object-to-benefactive wording explicit.

The Greek unless-perhaps exception formula is rendered unless ... actually. Both source particles supply the whole exception/evaluation construction, without treating the indefinite/emphatic component as a separate source lexical actually.

Greek you are unapproved is verbalized as you ... fail the test. The actual adjective and finite copula form this predicate across the intervening actually, which retains its own exception-formula group.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 opens the recognition question with or; BSB begins directly with Cant you see, without a separate or.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds a purpose explanation to Examine yourselves; no separate seeing verb or infinitive is written with examine at the start.
English supplies a copula in Jesus Christ is in you; this N1904 clause is verbless, while its earlier are and later are retain their actual separate sources.

13:6.sourceText: ἐλπίζω δὲ ὅτι γνώσεσθε ὅτι ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἐσμὲν ἀδόκιμοι.
13:6.targetText: And I hope you will realize that we have not failed the test.

groups.note: ἀδόκιμοι ("unapproved") is rendered failed the test.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the first ὅτι ("that") untranslated after hope.

13:7.sourceText: εὐχόμεθα δὲ πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν μὴ ποιῆσαι ὑμᾶς κακὸν μηδέν, οὐχ ἵνα ἡμεῖς δόκιμοι φανῶμεν, ἀλλ’ ἵνα ὑμεῖς τὸ καλὸν ποιῆτε, ἡμεῖς δὲ ὡς ἀδόκιμοι ὦμεν.
13:7.targetText: Now we pray to God that you will not do anything wrong—not that we will appear to have stood the test, but that you will do what is right, even if we appear to have failed.

groups.note: δόκιμοι ("approved") is rendered to have stood the test.
The article τό makes καλόν ("good") a noun, rendered what is right.
δέ ("but") is rendered as the concessive even if.
ὡς … ὦμεν ("be as") is rendered appear.
ἀδόκιμοι ("unapproved") is rendered to have failed.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the infinitive clause with that.
English supplies a copula in the phrase what is right.

13:8.sourceText: οὐ γὰρ δυνάμεθά τι κατὰ τῆς ἀληθείας, ἀλλὰ ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας.
13:8.targetText: For we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth.

groups.note: δύναμαι with an object ("be able for something") is rendered can do, so οὐ δυνάμεθα is rendered we cannot do.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds only; the Greek has ἀλλά alone.

13:9.sourceText: χαίρομεν γὰρ ὅταν ἡμεῖς ἀσθενῶμεν, ὑμεῖς δὲ δυνατοὶ ἦτε· τοῦτο καὶ εὐχόμεθα, τὴν ὑμῶν κατάρτισιν.
13:9.targetText: In fact, we rejoice when we are weak but you are strong, and our prayer is for your perfection.

groups.note: εὐχόμεθα ("we pray") is rendered our prayer is for.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves τοῦτο ("this") untranslated; your perfection names what is prayed for.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

13:10.sourceText: Διὰ τοῦτο ταῦτα ἀπὼν γράφω, ἵνα παρὼν μὴ ἀποτόμως χρήσωμαι κατὰ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἣν ὁ Κύριος ἔδωκέν μοι εἰς οἰκοδομὴν καὶ οὐκ εἰς καθαίρεσιν.
13:10.targetText: This is why I write these things while absent, so that when I am present I will not need to be severe in my use of the authority that the Lord gave me for building you up, not for tearing you down.

groups.note: διὰ τοῦτο ("because of this") is rendered This is why.
The participle παρών ("being present") is rendered when I am present.
χρήσωμαι ("I may use, deal") is rendered I will … my use.
κατά ("according to") is rendered in … of, framing my use of the authority.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB joins the two phrases without and.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in This is why.
A participle has no person; English supplies I.
English adds need to be; BSB turns the adverb ἀποτόμως ("severely") into the adjective severe.
English supplies the object; the Greek has the noun οἰκοδομή alone.
English supplies the object; the Greek has the noun καθαίρεσις alone.

13:11.sourceText: Λοιπόν, ἀδελφοί, χαίρετε, καταρτίζεσθε, παρακαλεῖσθε, τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖτε, εἰρηνεύετε, καὶ ὁ Θεὸς τῆς ἀγάπης καὶ εἰρήνης ἔσται μεθ’ ὑμῶν.
13:11.targetText: Finally, brothers, rejoice! Aim for perfect harmony, encourage one another, be of one mind, live in peace. And the God of love and peace will be with you.

groups.note: καταρτίζεσθε ("be restored, be made complete") is rendered Aim for perfect harmony.
τὸ αὐτό ("the same thing") is rendered one.
φρονεῖτε ("think") is rendered be of … mind.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB reads the middle παρακαλεῖσθε as reciprocal; the Greek has no reciprocal pronoun.

13:12.sourceText: Ἀσπάσασθε ἀλλήλους ἐν ἁγίῳ φιλήματι. Ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς οἱ ἅγιοι πάντες.
13:12.targetText: Greet one another with a holy kiss.

sourceMoved.reason: The Greek witness includes the saints greeting in 13:12; this edition prints it in 13:13. Exact source anchors are retained there.

review.note: The Greek witness combines the two English greetings in 13:12 and numbers the benediction 13:13. This translation divides the greetings into 13:12–13 and prints the benediction at 13:14. Actual Greek references are preserved.

13:13.sourceText: Ἡ χάρις τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἡ κοινωνία τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν.
13:13.targetText: All the saints send you greetings.

sourceMoved.reason: The benediction is Greek witness 13:13 and this edition 13:14. Its words are linked at the actual English benediction, not the greeting printed here.

review.note: The Greek witness combines the two English greetings in 13:12 and numbers the benediction 13:13. This translation divides the greetings into 13:12–13 and prints the benediction at 13:14. Actual Greek references are preserved.

13:14.sourceText: Ἡ χάρις τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἡ κοινωνία τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν.
13:14.targetText: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in this Greek nominal benediction; no separate Greek verb is written.

review.note: The Greek witness combines the two English greetings in 13:12 and numbers the benediction 13:13. This translation divides the greetings into 13:12–13 and prints the benediction at 13:14. Actual Greek references are preserved.
